content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary — INDEMN: deviation (targeting preferred).**

- **What exists:** Section 16.2 gives Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees an indemnity from Array, and Section 16.3 supplies a complete procedure (prompt written notice, Indemnitor sole control of defence/settlement, full cooperation) — those four elements are already met verbatim.
- **What fails:** Array's indemnity heads reach only Array-side commercialisation, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breach of Article 15 reps. There is **no third-party IP infringement indemnity** for the licensed Array Patents/Know-How or Array-supplied Products; Section 11.4 instead leaves each Subject Party to defend Infringement Actions "at its own expense", and Article 15 has no non-infringement warranty. No cover for Array's breach of Law, Array-caused disclosure of Ono Confidential Information, or Array's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and no express duty to defend. Ono's 16.1 indemnity is by contrast very broad — this is walk-away territory under the fallback.
- **Redline (validated ok:true, 4 ops):** (1) add "defend," to 16.2's lead-in; (2) insert one sentence adding the IP-infringement, breach-of-Law, data-disclosure and GN/WM heads, expressed "notwithstanding Section 11.4" so the retained own-expense defence mechanic does not contradict it; (3)–(4) narrow 16.1 to Ono-provided content and Ono's breach of Law. Section 16.3 is left untouched, so notice, control and cooperation carry over to the new heads without duplication.
